learning_extracted: Metric design must isolate the claim. approach_commit_rate aggregates over (beta_gate.is_elevated AND VALENCE_WANTING > threshold) -- in a substrate where multiple write paths populate VALENCE_WANTING (MECH-216, serotonin, MECH-290, MECH-307), the metric cannot dissociate MECH-295 contribution. The 490j sentinel demonstrates this directly: bridge is provably silent in ARM_0 (C6/C7=0 across all seeds) yet the metric still saturates at 1.0.

Severed-bridge baseline is necessary but not sufficient. Severing z_goal_enabled correctly disables MECH-295 at the source (C6/C7 zero in ARM_0 across all seeds, sentinel clean). But it does not disable the agent's other approach-related VALENCE_WANTING write paths. The 490i autopsy fixed one baseline contamination; 490j surfaces another at the readout layer.

The script's pre-registered ROW 3 routing prescription (parametric sweep on mech295_liking_to_approach_cue_gain and APPROACH_WANTING_THRESH) is misaligned with the actual failure mode. ROW 3's per-claim direction (narrow_supports) is correct; ROW 3's routing recommendation does not address ceiling-saturated negative controls. Future grids should distinguish 'C8 FAIL with ARM_0 near zero' from 'C8 FAIL with ARM_0 at ceiling'.

Substrate signal is genuinely strong. C6/C7/C9 PASS on 3/3 seeds with substantial magnitudes (peak anticipatory_write 0.287, peak approach_cue_bias 0.396, write_sum 80.2 vs zero in ARM_0) is more direct mechanistic support for MECH-295 weak-reading than any 490 cohort run prior. This signal should be weighted in governance via the narrow_supports per-claim direction.

Cohort-stable pattern across 490i + 490j: substrate-side direct measurements cleanly support MECH-295 weak-reading; every behavioural sign-test design tried so far has a distinct contamination (490i: goal_norm_peak baseline; 490j: approach_commit_rate ceiling). The next iteration must put a clean metric at the centre of the design, not just iterate on the baseline arm config.

routing_detail.queue-experiment: V3-EXQ-490k successor with corrected behavioural sign-test metric isolating MECH-295 contribution from non-MECH-295 VALENCE_WANTING writers. Three candidate designs (compose one or more): (a) action-class divergence on first commit tick between ARM_1 and ARM_0 holding other VALENCE_WANTING write paths matched (per-seed argmax-first-action ARM_1 != ARM_0 count or cosine distance on score_bias vector at first commit) -- tests whether MECH-295 changes the selected action, not whether VALENCE_WANTING aggregate is non-zero; (b) ablate non-MECH-295 VALENCE_WANTING writers in BOTH arms (schema_wanting_enabled=False, tonic_5ht_enabled=False, use_backward_credit_sweep=False, MECH-307 paths off) so approach_commit_rate reflects only MECH-295 contribution -- cleanest discriminant, but ablates substrates that may interact; (c) measure bridge-driven E3 score_bias propagation magnitude on first action selection directly (fraction of commit ticks where MECH-295 bridge per-candidate negative score_bias changes argmin from no-MECH-295-counterfactual to with-MECH-295) -- cleanest mechanistic isolation, most invasive instrumentation. Recommended composition: (a) + per-tick guard that confirms substrate is firing (C7 > floor) so metric only counts ticks where MECH-295 is actually producing bias; add variant (b) as a cross-validation ablation arm.
